The Moon is Earth’s sole natural satellite, orbiting about 384 000 km away and exerting roughly one‑sixth of Earth’s surface gravity. It drives the tides, helps stabilize our planet’s tilt, and the Apollo missions proved it’s a volcanic body by bringing back rock samples.
